Fi raqqin manshur (in an unrolled parchment): That is, in thin leather or unrolled paper.

Wa-l-Bayt al-Ma'mur (and the Frequented House): That is, filled with angels; seventy thousand angels enter it every day and never return.

Wa-s-saqf al-marfu' (and the raised roof): That is, the sky, which is like a raised roof over the earth.

Wa-l-bahr al-masjur (and the sea that is kindled): That is, the full, gathered sea whose water is joined one part to another.

Yawma tamuru s-sama'u mawra (the Day the sky will sway violently): That is, it will move and revolve.

Fi khawdin yal'abun (in vain talk they play): That is, in falsehood they play, occupying themselves with their disbelief.

Yud'awna ila nari jahannama da'a (they will be pushed toward the Fire of Hell with a push): That is, they will be shoved with violence.

Afasihrun hadha (Is this magic?): That is, this punishment you see, as you used to say about the Qur'an.

Am antum la tubsirun (or do you not see?): That is, or have you been deprived of sight, so that you do not see?

Isla-uha (burn in it): That is, roast in its heat.

Fasbiru aw la tasbiru (so be patient or be not patient): That is, your patience and its absence are equal for you.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted ﴿By the Mount, and by a Book inscribed, on parchment unrolled, and by the Frequented House, and by the raised roof, and by the swelling sea﴾: These are five great things by which Allah the Exalted swears. The words ﴿By the Mount﴾ refer to Mount Sinai (Jabal al-Tur) on which Allah the Exalted spoke to Musa, and it is a sanctified place. The words ﴿and by a Book inscribed, on parchment unrolled﴾ mean inscribed on paper or thin leather, and it is either the Torah or the Qur'an; the oath by it is because of the sanctity and holiness it has with Allah the Exalted. The Frequented House is a house in the heavens which the angels visit every day, filling it with worship; it is directly opposite the Ka'bah, such that if it were to fall, it would fall upon it. The raised roof is the sky, which is like a roof for the earth, and it is a manifestation of the power and knowledge of Allah the Exalted. The sea is likewise, and "masjur" means filled with enormous quantities of water; it is a manifestation of the divine power, knowledge and wisdom. The answer to this great oath, or the matter sworn to, is His saying: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord, O our Messenger, is bound to occur; there is none to repel it. It has no repeller who could ever push it away. It has a specific time in which it will occur, and signs that indicate it, which are the words of the Exalted ﴿On the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾, meaning it will move with intensity and revolve, and the mountains will move, becoming like scattered dust here and there. ﴿So woe on that Day to the deniers﴾. "Woe" (wayl) is a valley in Hell filled with the pus and blood of the people of the Fire. The deniers are those who disbelieve in Allah and in what His messengers brought from Him of the pillars of faith and the foundations of Islam. The words ﴿who are in vain talk, playing﴾ mean that they are engaged in their falsehood and disbelief, occupied with it away from true faith and righteous action that purifies the soul and cleanses it.

It will also be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿So be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you.﴾ That is, your patience and its absence are equal for you. ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾, that is, in the world, of shirk and sins.

**Explanation of the Words:**

**Indeed, the righteous (al-muttaqin):** those who fear their Lord, worship Him alone in the way He prescribed, perform the obligatory duties (al-fara'id), and avoid what He forbade (al-nawahi).

**Fruit-enjoying (fakihin):** those who take delight in eating the abundant fruits their Lord has given them.

**And He protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire (wa waqahum 'adhab al-jahim):** He safeguarded them from the torment of the Fire, the punishment of the Blaze.

**On couches arranged in rows (surar masfufah):** some of them placed beside one another.

**And We gave them in marriage to wide-eyed houris (wa zawwajnahum bi-hur 'in):** We joined them with women of large, beautiful eyes.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

When the Exalted mentioned the state of the people of the Fire, He mentioned the state of the people of Paradise. This is the method of encouragement and warning (al-targhib wa al-tarhib) for which the Noble Qur'an is distinguished. So the Exalted said, informing about the state of the people of Paradise: ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, that is, those who guarded themselves in this world against polytheism and sins, ﴿will be in gardens﴾, that is, orchards and enduring bliss, encompassing everything delightful and pleasant that souls desire and eyes take pleasure in. ﴿Enjoying what their Lord has given them﴾, that is, taking delight in eating abundant fruits, described by the saying of God the Exalted: neither cut off nor forbidden. ﴿And their Lord has protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, that is, He kept them safe from the torment of the Fire. And it will be said to them: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you used to do﴾, that is, because of what you used to do of righteous deeds and reform, in addition to the obligatory duties and avoiding polytheism and sins. His saying ﴿reclining﴾ means that, while they are in their bliss, they recline on couches arranged in rows, some placed beside others. And His saying the Exalted ﴿and We will marry them to wide-eyed houris﴾, that is, We will join them with wives from among the houris (al-hur al-'in). The word hur is the plural of hawra', a woman in whom the whiteness of the eye predominates over its blackness, and 'in is the plural of 'ayna', a woman with large eyes. May God make us among those who are married to them; indeed, He is Generous.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The excellence of piety and the honor of its people.
2. Explanation of God's favor and grace upon the believers and the pious, who are God's close friends (awliya').

Rather, righteous deeds purify the soul, making its owner fit to enter Paradise. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 52, verses 21–28:

Explanation of the words:

"Those who believed" (wa-alladhina amanu): i.e., with true faith, which entails Islam and excellence (ihsan).

"And their offspring followed them in faith" (wa-attaba'athum dhurriyyatuhum bi-iman): i.e., with complete faith that fulfils its conditions, among them Islam.

"We will join their offspring with them" (alhaqna bihim dhurriyyatahum): i.e., even if they did not perform their deeds but fell short in that.

"And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds" (wa-ma alatnahum min 'amalihim min shay'): i.e., and We did not diminish for them anything from the rewards of their deeds.

"Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned" (kull mri'in bima kasaba rahin): i.e., every human being is held as a pledge, that is, confined by his false earnings.

"They will pass around therein a cup" (yatanaza'una fiha ka'san): i.e., they will hand to one another in it, that is, in Paradise, a cup of wine.

"No ill speech therein, nor sinfulness" (la laghwa fiha wa-la ta'thim): i.e., no idle talk will occur for them because of drinking it, and idle talk is every speech with no good and no sin in it.

"And there will go around them boys" (wa-yatufu 'alayhim ghilman): i.e., servants for them will circulate among them.

"As if they were pearls well-guarded" (ka'annahum lu'lu'un maknun): i.e., preserved.

"And they will turn to one another, questioning" (wa-aqbala ba'duhum 'ala ba'din yatasa'alun): i.e., some of them will ask others about what they were in the world and what they have reached in the Hereafter.

"They will say: Indeed we were before" (qalu inna kunna qabl): i.e., they said, pointing to the cause of their happiness: indeed we were before, that is, in the world.

"Among our people, fearful" (fi ahlina mushfiqin): i.e., among our families and children, fearful, that is, afraid of the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.

"So Allah has bestowed favour upon us" (fa-manna Allahu 'alayna): i.e., with forgiveness.

"And protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind" (wa-waqana 'adhab al-samum): i.e., and preserved us from the punishment of the Fire whose heat penetrates the pores of the body.

"Indeed we used to call upon Him" (inna kunna nad'uhu): i.e., in the world we worshipped Him, affirming His oneness.

"Indeed, He is the Good, the Merciful" (innahu huwa al-barr al-rahim): i.e., the Benevolent, who is true to His promise, the Merciful, the One of great mercy.

As for His statement, exalted is He: "And there will go around them boys" (wa-yatufu 'alayhim ghilman), i.e., servants for them, who in their beauty and fine appearance are like pearls well-guarded in their shells.

As for His statement, exalted is He: "And they will turn to one another, questioning" (wa-aqbala ba'duhum 'ala ba'din yatasa'alun), i.e., about what they had in the world and what they have reached in the Hereafter of this everlasting bliss. Indeed we were before, i.e., in the world before the Hereafter, calling upon Him and humbling ourselves before Him that He would protect us from the Fire and admit us to Paradise. Indeed, He is exalted, the Benevolent toward His friends, the Merciful toward His believing servants.

1- A complete description of the people of Paradise, which at the same time affirms the Resurrection and the recompense by mentioning what takes place in it.

2- The excellence of faith and the honour of its people with Allah, by joining the offspring who had little righteous deeds to their fathers who had abundant righteous deeds.

5- The excellence of supplication and humble entreaty to Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 52, verses 35–43:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Am khuliqu min ghayri shay'?﴾ (Were they created from nothing?): that is, were they created without any creator? This is false.

﴿Am hum al-khaliqun?﴾ (Or are they the creators?): that is, of themselves? This is impossible, since a thing's existence cannot precede its own existence.

﴿Am khalaqu as-samawati wal-ard?﴾ (Or did they create the heavens and the earth?): that is, they did not create them, because their inability to create themselves proves their inability to create others.

﴿Bal la yuqinun﴾ (Rather, they do not have certainty): that is, that Allah created them and created the heavens and the earth, as they themselves say. For had they been certain, they would not have worshipped other than Allah, and they would have believed in His Messenger ﷺ.

﴿Am 'indahum khaza'inu rabbik﴾ (Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord?): that is, of provision, prophethood and other things, so that they could give these to whomever they wish among people.

﴿Am hum al-musaytirun﴾ (Or are they the controllers?): that is, the dominant, overpowering ones who dispose of matters as they wish.

﴿Am lahum sullamun yastami'una fihi﴾ (Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?): that is, do they have a means of ascent to the heaven by which they climb, hear the speech of the angels, bring it back, and oppose the Messenger in his words?

﴿Fal-ya'tu bi-sultanin mubin﴾ (Then let them bring a clear authority): that is, a clear proof demonstrating his truthfulness. They have none of this at all.

﴿Am lahu al-banatu wa lakum al-banun?﴾ (Has He daughters while you have sons?): that is, Allah has daughters and you have sons. All your statements of this kind have no reality whatsoever; they are fabrications.

﴿Am tas'aluhum ayyuha ar-rasulu ajran?﴾ (Or do you ask them, O Messenger, for a reward?): that is, for conveying your call.
